title: A hundred glorifications
hook: glory to Allah and praise to Him, a hundred times, wiping sins like sea foam (Bukhari)
tomorrow: why does the morning line call sleep a kind of death?

segments.voice: Yesterday, radiitu: pleased with Allah as Lord, glad of what you belong to. Pleased. A new week starts with a woman who didn't leave her prayer place all morning.

On a beach, the tide leaves a long line of foam, bright white along the sand, and the next wave takes most of it away. Hold that picture. Now a room at dawn. Juwayriya, one of the Prophet's wives, sits down at her place of prayer to remember God. He goes out. The sun climbs. Midmorning, he comes back, and she's still there, in the same spot. He asks: you've been here, just as I left you? She says yes. And he tells her something she can't have expected. Since I left you, he says, I said four phrases, three times, that would outweigh everything you've said all morning.
screen: `A LINE OF FOAM ON THE SAND.` → `STILL IN HER PLACE AT MIDMORNING.` → `FOUR PHRASES, THREE TIMES.`

segments.voice: The phrases begin: subhanallahi wa bihamdihi, glory to Allah and His is the praise. Then: as many as His creation, as much as pleases Him, as heavy as His throne, as endless as the ink of His words. That's in Sahih Muslim. Not a hundred. Three, with the whole world folded inside them. Now the hundred. In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ says whoever says subhanallahi wa bihamdihi a hundred times in a day has their sins wiped away, even if they are like the foam of the sea. That answers yesterday's question, and it's the picture to tell a friend tonight. Foam looks like a lot. It covers the whole shore. And it's the lightest thing on it: one wave, and it's gone. The two hadiths aren't rivals. They're two doors into the same words. One says: say it a hundred times, steadily, through a day. The other says: say it, and mean everything by it. The story never says Juwayriya's morning was wasted. It shows how much one phrase can hold. Counted out, a hundred fits into a few minutes. Meant fully, three can fill a lifetime. Like the sea's foam.
screen: `FOUR PHRASES, THREE TIMES.` · `A HUNDRED, THROUGH A DAY.` · `THE LIGHTEST THING ON THE SHORE.` · `TWO DOORS, SAME WORDS.` · then, large: `LIKE THE SEA'S FOAM.`

segments.voice: Use the joints of your fingers to count, the way some Muslims do, thumb touching each segment in turn. With each one, say silently, subhanallahi wa bihamdihi, or simply 'glory', as far as the sit allows. Don't race toward a hundred; let each one land light.
screen: `COUNT ON YOUR FINGERS.` · `ONE PHRASE PER JOINT.` · `LET EACH ONE LAND LIGHT.`

segments.voice: A hundred glorifications: subhanallahi wa bihamdihi, said a hundred times in a day, and sins wiped away like the sea's foam.
Your line: like the sea's foam. It looks like everything, and one wave takes it. Glory, counted.

howItsDone: Muslims say subhanallahi wa bihamdihi through the day, counting on their fingers or on prayer beads (a tasbih), and some keep the hundred as a daily practice.
